messages:
From: Elena Rossi <elena.rossi@novamed.com>

Cc: contracts@novamed.com

Subject: Initial redlines and request: retrofit fee reassignment + SOW split

Diego / Marissa,

Thanks again for the demo last week — team liked the latency improvements. We've attached our preferred redlines to the order form and a proposed SOW split into Phase A (pilot) and Phase B (production). Two items we need to lock down before procurement can approve:

- Reassign the retrofit fee from Exhibit A into a one-time implementation credit applied against month 1 invoice.
- Split the SOW so that Phase A (limited data residency) is timeboxed and priced separately; Phase B should be contingent on acceptance criteria in Exhibit C.

I've attached: Novamed_OrderForm_v3_redline.docx and SOW-PhaseA_v2.pdf. Please confirm whether Redwood legal needs a different rev format and send an updated pricing sheet (we also asked finance to run a cost-model but wanted your confirmation on the credit).

If we can get this to legal by EOD Thursday (05/06) procurement will target signature week of 05/17.

Thanks,
Elena Rossi
Head of AI Platforms
NovaMed

Attachments: Novamed_OrderForm_v3_redline.docx (docx - redline), SOW-PhaseA_v2.pdf (pdf)

From: Diego Fernandez <diego_fernandez@redwood.com>

Subject: Re: Initial redlines and request: retrofit fee reassignment + SOW split

Thanks Elena — looping in Marissa (AM) and Laura (legal) and Connor (pricing ops). Quick read: their redline removes the retrofit as a separate line item and replaces it with an implementation credit equal to 25% of month 1 fees; SOW split is straightforward but we need to tighten acceptance criteria for Phase A.

Laura — can you review the attached redline and advise whether we can accept the reclassification of the retrofit fee as a credit (commercially acceptable?) and whether the conditional language on Phase B needs additional liability language. Also call out any DocuSign or counterparty signature order preferences.

Connor — if we agree to the credit, can you prepare an updated cost-model (xlsx) showing month 1 with credit applied and the overall ARR impact for the first 12 months? Elena wants to show procurement the net-effect.

Target: legal comments back by 05/04 COB, commercial pricing update by 05/05 AM, then I will collate and propose a final redline to Elena for signature flow.

—Diego

Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Initial redlines and request: retrofit fee reassignment + SOW split

Diego / team,

Thanks — reviewed the Novamed redlines (attached my annotated version: Novamed_OrderForm_v3_legal_comments.docx). High level:

1) Reclassifying the retrofit fee as a one-time implementation credit is acceptable if we add a short carveout clarifying the credit applies only after the customer executes the amended order form and the SOW Phase A acceptance criteria are met. Without that carveout we expose Redwood to a pre-pay/credit risk if the customer cancels before onboarding.

2) For the SOW split: Phase A must have explicit acceptance tests (dataset ingest window, latency threshold, false positive rate on our sample tests). I added placeholders in Exhibit C and flagged them for Marissa to align with the POA. Phase B should include a rollback provision in case data residency requirements change.

3) Liability/indemnity: NovaMed's redline adds language limiting Redwood's right to use aggregated telemetry for performance tuning. We should accept aggregated, de-identified telemetry; added a short clause that allows telemetry for operational improvements but prohibits sharing customer-identifiable data.

4) Signature flow: prefer Redwood signs first (to ensure internal billing setup) then NovaMed executes; DocuSign envelope should include Order Form first, then Exhibit C (SOW Phase A) as separate attachments so procurement can sign in order. I've added a DocuSign note in the tracked doc.

I'm attaching my marked doc and a short redline summary. If commercial wants to proceed on the credit, ask Connor to update the model and then we can insert the credit calculation clause (I suggested a one-line formula in Section 2.3).

Laura Bennett
Sr. Counsel, Commercial Contracts
Redwood Inference

Attachments: Novamed_OrderForm_v3_legal_comments.docx (docx - legal comments), legal-summary.txt

From: Diego Fernandez <diego_fernandez@redwood.com>
To: Elena Rossi <elena.rossi@novamed.com>, contracts@novamed.com
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>, Connor O'Brien <connor_obrien@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 05 May 2027 15:46:00 -0700
Subject: Finalizing flow: retrofit credit formula + DocuSign route (next steps)

Elena / NovaMed contracts team — thanks for the quick turnaround. Per our internal review here's the agreed approach and next steps: 

1) Commercial: We will accept the retrofit reclassification as a one-time implementation credit equal to 25% of Month 1 invoice, applied as a line-credit on invoice #1. Connor attached the updated cost-model (cost-model-sheet.xlsx) to illustrate the net impact.

2) Legal carveouts: Redwood will add a clause that the credit is only applied post-execution of the amended order form and successful Phase A acceptance tests. Redwood will preserve the right to use aggregated, de-identified telemetry for performance tuning.

3) SOW split: Phase A (Pilot) will be limited to 90 days with acceptance criteria in Exhibit C. Phase B (Production) will be scoped and priced separately and contingent on acceptance. We included a rollback/transition clause for data residency changes.

4) Signature flow & timeline: Redwood will send a DocuSign envelope today with the Order Form (amended) first, then Exhibit C (Phase A SOW) attached. Redwood signs first; NovaMed signs second. Target signature by 05/17 so onboarding can start week of 05/24. DocuSign link: https://www.docusign.com/space/embedded-sign/abc123-novamed-orderform

Elena — if that matches NovaMed's procurement expectations please confirm and indicate the preferred purchaser contact for any PO paperwork (we'll route final invoice sequencing once signed).

Thanks — I'll follow up once the envelope is out.

—Diego Fernandez
Director, Strategic Accounts
Redwood Inference
